A Consumer Insight Report

How to Win Over Gen Z

Ethan Yoo

Scroll
01
Introduction

Who is Gen Z?

Born roughly between 1997–2012 — grew up during global unrest, financial crises, the COVID-19 pandemic, climate anxiety, and the advent of AI.

Known as "digital natives" since they were the first ones to grow up with the Internet.

They dominate video sharing platforms, seek out their niche interests and communities, and prioritize curating their online identity.

Known for their idealism: demanding purpose and accountability, opportunities for the marginalized, sustainability, mental health awareness, etc.

Values self expression but also tend to chase trends to feel apart of the "in-group."

02
The Core Insight

Gen Z responds best to messages that feel authentic and credible to the brand's purpose

Algorithmic feeds have overexposed Gen Z to branded content, making them seek out inspiration among a landscape of noise.

Gen Z can tell when brands are performing an act for approval, and it comes off as out of touch.

Brands have to meet the people where they are, rather than the brands being the center of attention.

03
Section 1

Relatability Wins

Authenticity is one of the highest valued traits for a generation that embraces quirks and unique imperfections

The Reasons Why

Gen Z grew up in the age of influencer marketing, content creators, flashy editing and vivid thumbnails which means they don't automatically trust something just because it has good production quality.

When content feels like its pushing an agenda, it turns off Gen Z, who have learned to recognize brand voice and sniff out the facade.

Reducing the perceived agenda by avoiding over editing and embracing imperfections makes content more palatable as it feels more human.

Content that feels spontaneous, uses ordinary people, and everyday equipment feels more personal.

04
Section 2

Attention Economy

Scrolling and short-form content have made it so that brands have to compete harder for attention

The Reasons Why

The average person sees 6,000 ads a day, with only 0.3% being remembered, which makes recall even more valuable than reach.

Some brands choose to make their messaging and tone chaotic/unhinged to stand out from other brands while also fitting in with Gen Z humor and memes.

Content has to grab attention in the first few seconds, because the constant flow of information makes it so that audiences are constantly looking for novelty.

Algorithms reward content with high engagement, so brands need to make people want to engage and feel that the brand is worth their attention.

05
Section 3

Speak Their Language

Humor has quickly become central in how brands reach and connect with the younger generation

The Reasons Why

Meme culture and inside jokes have become a shared language for Gen Z to express opinions, react to cultural events, and connect online.

Cultural fluency is needed since jokes are extremely layered, context is assumed, and almost nonsensical to someone out of the loop.

Play along and be okay with being the focus of jokes because fighting against it feels defensive and guilty.

Gen Z need to be entertained before being fully convinced of a product/company since it makes the marketing more palatable through shared language and culture.

06
Section 4

Part of the Community

Brands have to demonstrate that they belong with their audience and make them feel seen

The Reasons Why

Gen Z uses the internet to express their identity and find like-minded people, creating countless niche communities with their own subcultures.

Successful marketing has shifted from reaching as many people as possible to focusing on finding the right people.

Micro-trends and data driven curation has made Gen Z more skeptical of buying a product purely by discovering it.

Audiences seek out emotional connections and interactions with brands they shop with.

07
Section 5

Talk the Talk, Walk the Walk

Corporate social responsibility is a non-negotiable, and companies need to prove that they care

The Reasons Why

Gen Z believes that companies need to make a positive social impact to be worth supporting.

A company's actions must reflect its purpose and values because messaging is not enough — brands need to show receipts.

Gen Z is constantly thinking about purpose and want to feel part of a good cause when supporting a company.

Work culture and leadership behavior also impact the perception of the brand.

08
Section 6

Building Trust & Credibility

The relationship between brands and audiences has shifted from transactional to reciprocal

The Reasons Why

Brands have to be willing to evolve with their consumers because brand loyalty is no longer about repeated purchases.

Trust and credibility are hard to come by for Gen Z because they are inherently skeptical of a company's motives.

User-generated content (UGC) is extremely valuable in building a relationship between brands and audiences because Gen Z is quicker to believe people they relate to.

UGC offers a way for audiences to engage with the brand post-purchase and remain part of the brand's story.

Consumers expect brands to listen and engage with their communities.

09
Section 7

Navigating Platforms

Different platforms require different styles of messaging since each one serves a different purpose for users

The Reasons Why

Gen Z treats different social platforms as tools for their respective purposes — TikTok for short form entertainment, Instagram as a personal visual blog, YouTube for long form content, and X/Twitter for real-time reactions.

Brands need to be aware of which ideas/strategies work for each platform because the content needs to fit in with the feed.

The content/message doesn't need to change between platforms, but the tone and presentation might have to.

10
Takeaways

What Should Brands Do?

Forming a Connection

Cultural fluency is essential to keep up with trends, pop culture, headlines, memes, etc. Establish a two-way relationship with the community through social media engagement, experiential popups, and evolve with them. Elevate the voices of UGC creators and everyday consumers to build trust. Understand your niche/community, what they value, and participate in their shared culture.


Be Real and Authentic

Prioritize authenticity over corporate polish because high production quality isn't guaranteed to earn credibility anymore. Entertain audiences, grab attention instantly, and fit into their feeds by acting like a content creator rather than a brand. Prove your worth to your audience and avoid empty promises through the actions of the brand.

11
Examples and Conclusion

Gen Z hates performance.

Brands that are confident, transparent, and reflect who their audience is build the strongest connections with Gen Z.

Duolingo

The bird mascot has been turned into a personality (started from memes).

Reacts to and references pop culture moments and topics for engagement.

Content is entertaining and relatable which makes it easily fit into feeds.

Nike

Partners with popular athletes and personalities.

Not just about the product, but it represents a culture/niche.

Consistent messaging and storytelling has built trust with their audience.

Spotify

Centered around user experience, discovery, and identity curation.

Wrapped allows users to share their identity and niche with style.

Evolved with their audience by bringing in podcasts and audiobooks.
